topStories.headline: Four Clarion Alley Murals Painted Over; Artists Race to Restore Them Before Memory Fades
topStories.dek: A property management company whitewashed four murals on August 24, and the Clarion Alley Mural Project is now fundraising $35,000 to rebuild the lost work.
topStories.body:
Four murals in Clarion Alley — the Mission District's one-block open-air gallery connecting Mission and Valencia streets between 17th and 18th — were painted white on August 24 when a crew sent by Makras Real Estate Group covered them while responding to what the company said was a graffiti complaint. Three murals were completely obliterated; a fourth was partially obscured before an artist who witnessed the whitewashing persuaded the worker to stop. The Clarion Alley Mural Project (CAMP), the volunteer nonprofit that has managed the alley's more than 50 works since 1992, said it received no warning before the incident.

Among the destroyed works was a memorial to San Francisco activist Kirsten Brydum. Nyia Luna, an artist with Graffiti Camp for Girls whose mural was painted over in 2026, said she had spent hours designing the piece. CAMP co-director Veronica Torres met with the office of District 9 Supervisor Jackie Fielder, whose staff has offered to assist with restoration efforts and longer-term care of the space.

The destruction exposed a structural tension in how the city handles graffiti abatement: San Francisco Public Works spends more than $20 million annually on graffiti removal and can fine property owners $362 plus cleanup costs if they fail to act within 30 days — yet the city's own abatement guidelines do not protect or restore tagged murals. CAMP launched a $35,000 fundraiser to cover restoration costs and sustain operations for the coming year. As of the most recent reports, restoration painting was expected to begin imminently, and only one wall had been reclaimed so far.

topStories.headline: Hit-and-Run Driver Strikes Pedestrian at Mission and Park Streets in Bernal Heights, Flees Scene
topStories.dek: A pedestrian is in critical condition after being struck Saturday night near the Mission-Bernal corridor; SFPD is asking the public for tips.
topStories.body:
A pedestrian was left with life-threatening injuries Saturday evening, September 20, after being struck by a vehicle at the intersection of Mission and Park streets in Bernal Heights. The driver fled the scene and had not been located as of the most recent police update. San Francisco police said officers responded at approximately 8:18 p.m. to a vehicle collision involving a pedestrian, and the case remains an open and active investigation.

The crash adds to a troubling trend documented by the city's own transportation agency. A July report from the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency found that severe-injury collisions in the first half of 2026 had increased by roughly 8 percent compared to the same period in 2025, with more than 300 traffic crashes resulting in pedestrian injuries so far this year.

Anyone with information about the Bernal Heights hit-and-run is asked to contact SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411, beginning the message with the letters SFPD.

topStories.headline: Applications Now Open for 35 Affordable Units at 3300 Mission Street — Deadline Is October 6
topStories.dek: The nearly complete six-story building on the Mission-Bernal corridor will house low-income residents, but an unexpected PG&E infrastructure upgrade has complicated the timeline.
topStories.body:
Applications are open through October 6, 2026, for 3300 Mission Street, a 35-unit, 100 percent affordable housing development on the Mission-Bernal corridor — the first such project in the neighborhood in nearly 20 years. The six-story building, developed by a partnership of three Black-led organizations (Bernal Heights Housing Corporation, Tabernacle Community Development Corporation, and Mitchelville Real Estate Group), will serve individuals and small households earning between 30 and 80 percent of the area median income. Approximately 40 percent of the apartments are set aside for households who live in District 9, within a half-mile of the property, or have been displaced from housing in San Francisco.

The project replaced the site of the former 3300 Club and the Graywood Hotel, which were destroyed in a 2016 fire. Construction broke ground in November 2024. The building was originally expected to be complete in summer 2026, but an unexpected expansion of the project's PG&E electrical infrastructure work — required to serve a broader portion of Bernal Heights — has quadrupled the electrical budget and may extend the delivery timeline, according to a May 2026 update from Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center. The ground floor will include retail space; BHNC is also seeking a commercial tenant for a prime corner location at Mission and 29th Street.

Interested applicants can reach the leasing team through the Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center at 3300mission@bhnc.org.

events.title: COCOON: An Orchestra Sleepover Concert
events.location: Gray Area / Grand Theater, 2665 Mission St, Mission District
events.description: Magik*Magik Orchestra presents San Francisco's first-ever orchestra sleepover concert, with attendees sleeping on camping cots surrounded by live strings, winds, horns, and voice. A final 26-minute composition is timed to end at the moment of sunrise — 7:01 AM on September 27.

events.title: 3300 Mission Street Affordable Housing — Application Deadline
events.description: Last day to apply for one of 35 studio apartments at the new 100% affordable development on the Mission-Bernal corridor, serving households earning 30–80% of area median income. About 40% of units are reserved for District 9 residents or San Francisco displacement cases.

events.title: Valencia LIVE! — October Street Party
events.location: Valencia Street between 18th and 21st Streets, Mission District
events.description: The final Valencia LIVE! of the 2026 season closes out the monthly free street celebration with live music curated by Carnaval SF, cocktails to go from participating businesses, art, and shopping in the newly designated Valencia Street Entertainment Zone.
events.sourceName: Funcheap SF / Valencia Corridors Merchants Association

events.title: Balmy Alley Mural Restoration — Work Underway
events.location: Balmy Alley (between 24th and 25th streets), Mission District
events.description: A team of original muralists, funded by a $129,294 Community Challenge Grant from the city, is restoring six historic murals in Balmy Alley after Arts Commission design approvals; work was expected to begin in September. A separate Avenue Greenlight grant is also funding a partial restoration of the Women's Building's iconic 'Maestrapeace' mural on 18th Street.

moreNews.headline: Valencia Street Is Now a Full-Time Entertainment Zone — Open-Container Rules Apply Every Day
moreNews.body: As of May 2026, when Mayor Lurie signed legislation creating five new entertainment zones and the city published its Valencia Street management plan, the stretch of Valencia between 16th and 21st Streets became an active entertainment zone seven days a week from noon to midnight. Bars and restaurants may sell alcoholic beverages to go for outdoor consumption during those hours on any day of the year, subject to standard ABC permit conditions. The designation followed months of advocacy from the Valencia Corridors Merchants Association and was co-sponsored in the Board of Supervisors by District 9 Supervisor Jackie Fielder.

moreNews.headline: SFUSD School Board Race Heats Up Ahead of November 3 General Election
moreNews.body: Three seats on the San Francisco Unified School District board are on the November 3, 2026, general election ballot, with the race drawing sharp lines between progressive and moderate slates. Mission Local has been tracking the field weekly; the race features GrowSF, the teachers union, and the Parent Coalition as major organized forces. Non-citizen parents of SFUSD students are eligible to vote in the school board contest. Voter registration information is available at sf.gov.

restaurants.name: Royal Cuckoo Organ Bar

shops.name: City Art Gallery & Co-op

shops.name: Bi-Rite Creamery

shops.name: Dandelion Chocolate
shops.description: A craft chocolate maker on Valencia Street that sources cacao directly from farms and makes each bar in small batches on-site, with a factory store open to visitors.

shops.type: Mural arts center and gift shop

artEntertainment.description: The lovingly restored 1916 New Mission Theatre, now a dine-in cinema screening first-run and repertory films with a full menu and cocktails served in-seat.

artEntertainment.name: Foreign Cinema (Courtyard Screenings)

artEntertainment.name: Precita Eyes Muralists
